senses.gloss:
Nāciketāgni
(‘the fire of नचिकेतस्’)
------------------------------------------
In the story of नचिकेतस् as described in the Kaṭha Upaniṣad, the second boon that the young boy नचिकेतस् asked from यम, the god of death, was about the sacrifice (in fire) that could help one to attain स्वर्ग or हेअवेन् after death.
Yama taught him the same, in all its details and tested him at the end, just to know whether he had rightly comprehended this difficult subject. When he got excellent answers यम was so pleased with नचिकेतस् that he christened the sacrifice itself and the main fire in it, as ‘Nāciketāgni.’
The details of the sacrifice, however, are not known.
See also KAṬHA UPANIṢAD.
